In addition, there is no IP model in place that allows for open or third-party knowledge sharing, outside of open source development licenses, with each lab requiring independent review of such agreements. General-use open source licenses tend to require internal review as well, with highly complex copyright requirements that don’t make sense for successful, long-term collaboration. This is particularly true of products that use software libraries with commercial usage restrictions or copy-left requirements. Creating software projects without consideration of such restrictions can immediately freeze certain industrial or academic partners from involvement before even considering the creation of a collaboration.
